chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far and others, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah — all together — from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Musadif who said:

A man from our brethren fell gravely ill in Mecca until he was near death. We met Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) on the road, and he said: 'O Musadif, what happened to so-and-so?' I said, 'I left him near death, may I be your sacrifice.' He said: 'Had I been in your place, I would have given him water from the Mizab (the spout of the Ka'bah) to drink.'

So we sought it from everyone but could not find any. While we were in this situation, suddenly a cloud appeared with thunder, lightning, and rain. I went to someone in the mosque, gave him a dirham, and took his drinking cup. Then I took water from the Mizab, brought it to him and gave him to drink from it. I did not leave his side until he had drunk sawiq and recovered, and he was cured after that.

key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: A formula of deep reverence: 'may I be your ransom/sacrifice', used by companions when addressing the Imams
key_terms.سَوِيق: Sawiq — a traditional nourishing drink made from roasted barley or wheat flour; commonly used as a restorative food
key_terms.مَاءُ الْمِيزَابِ: Water of the Mizab — the golden spout installed on the Ka'bah that directs rainwater; considered blessed and curative

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of water from the Mizab (spout) of the Ka'bah in Islamic tradition?
ai.summary: Musadif, a companion of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), narrates a miraculous account of healing through the water of the Mizab (the golden spout of the Ka'bah). When a sick brother was near death in Mecca, the Imam prescribed water from the Mizab as a cure. After they could not find any, providence sent rain that filled the Mizab, and the man was healed after drinking it. This hadith highlights the baraka (blessing) associated with sacred sites of the Ka'bah and the Imam's knowledge of remedies.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, and someone else, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, altogether, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Yahya Bin Al Mubarak, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Musadif who said,

‘A man from our brethren complained at Makkah until he fell for the death. So we met Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> in the street, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Musadif! What did you do with so and so?’ I said, ‘I left him with the death, may I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But had I<sup>asws</sup> been in your place, I<sup>asws</sup> would have quenched him from the water of the groove (of the Kabah)’.

So we sought with everyone, but we did not find it. So whilst we were indulged in that, when a cloud raised itself, so there was thunder and lightning and it rained. So I went over to someone in the Masjid, so I gave him one Dirham and took his drinking cup. Then I took from the water of the groove and came up with it and quenched him from it, and I did not go away from his presence until he had drunk Saweyq, and was healthy, and he was cured after that’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ja‘far and other and certain persons of our people from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah all from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah from Musadif who has said the following:

“Once in Makkah one of our brothers (in belief) fell ill and was near death. We met abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, on the way and he (the Imam) asked, ‘O Musadif, how is so and so doing?’ I replied, ‘I left him for death, I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Were I in your place I would make him drink water from al-Mizab.’

We then searched if anyone had such water but we did not find it. At this time, a cloud rose with thunder and lightning. I then went to those in al-Masjid, gave a dirham and took a bowl from someone, then took water from al-Mizab, took it to our patient, made him drink from it and I still was with him that he began drinking sawiq. He became well and in good health.’”
